proposal_rules.title: Task-Scoped Patch Scope Overrides Default Date Sync
proposal_rules.hypothesis: Unexpected-write failures occur when default cross-record sync rules are applied even when task-scoped audit metadata explicitly narrows the patch scope and defers cleanup.
proposal_rules.change: Add a precedence rule: when task-provided audit/context metadata explicitly marks a focused patch scope and deferred cleanup, that scope overrides default reminder-account date synchronization for the current task. Add a pre-write scope gate requiring the agent to derive an allowed write set from instruction plus task-scoped docs, and skip consistency-only writes outside that set.

proposal_rules.title: Add Outbox Sequence Consistency Gate
proposal_rules.hypothesis: When `outbox/seq.json` and observed numbered outbox files are inconsistent, blindly trusting one source can cause writes to scorer-disallowed paths; requiring a pre-write consistency check and clarification fallback will reduce unexpected-write failures.
proposal_rules.change: Add a compact preflight rule for email tasks: before writing `outbox/*.json`, compute `seq_id` from `outbox/seq.json` and `max_existing_id` from numeric outbox filenames. Proceed with mutation only when `seq_id == max_existing_id + 1` and the target file does not already exist. If not, do not write outbox files and return `OUTCOME_NONE_CLARIFICATION` with a minimal sequencing question.

proposal_rules.title: Grounding Ref Coverage Gate for Entity-Filtered Answers
proposal_rules.hypothesis: When a query filters by a person/entity (especially with name-order variants), answering from downstream records alone can omit the canonical identity file and trigger reference-mismatch failures.
proposal_rules.change: Add a pre-`report_completion` gate: for person/entity-filtered outputs, require grounding refs to include (1) the canonical identity source used to resolve the filter (for CRM tasks, relevant `contacts/*` manager/contact file) and (2) the files used to produce the returned rows. If the prompt uses reordered/variant name tokens, resolve identity via canonical record first, then derive result rows.
